decision_reason: The reporting directly connects a measured statewide benefit-participation decline with provider-reported demand growth.

dedupe_assessment.continued_condition_assessment: No match was found on any required duplicate surface. The review preserves that the statewide participation decline has multiple possible causes and that provider demand was not reported as one statewide percentage.

measurable_change.description: Florida SNAP participation has fallen roughly 20 percent since July 2025, while Central Florida food-assistance providers report increased demand. United Against Poverty in Orlando reports increased new grocery-program memberships, including families with children. Second Harvest of Central Florida reports greater need than at the same time last year and currently distributes food equivalent to about 300,000 meals per day.

event_assessment.service: SNAP assistance and emergency grocery and food-bank programs.

causal.note: The participation decline is documented in current USDA-derived reporting, but participation counts alone cannot establish why every former participant left SNAP. Federal eligibility changes are one documented factor, and the report provides a direct recent loss example, but the statewide causal split among eligibility changes, administrative churn, income changes and other factors is not quantified. The statewide participation decline does not establish why every former participant left SNAP. Current reporting identifies tighter eligibility rules as one factor but does not quantify their exact contribution. Provider demand increases are directly reported but not expressed as a single percentage increase.
